newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil re-election bill has Senate support - poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazil re-election bill has Senate support - poll.

text.p: A bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year has widespread support in the Senate which has to vote on it, an opinion poll published on Sunday said.

A poll of the upper house's 81 members found 61 favoured a constitutional amendment that would give sitting presidents, state governors and mayors the chance of a second, consecutive term, O Globo and O Estado de Sao Paulo newspapers said.

The amendment would allow re-election in Brazil for the first time since the founding of the Republic in 1889. It was approved in a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies last week and faces another lower house vote before going to the Senate.
Forty-nine senators -- equivalent to a three-fifths majority -- must vote in favour of the bill in each of two votes in the upper house for the reform to be approved.
The poll, which was appeared in both newspapers, said 13 senators opposed the bill, four had not made up their minds and three did not indicate how they intended to vote.

The poll represented another boost for Cardoso's bid to become Brazil's first re-elected president. He pulled off the biggest victory of his current term on Tuesday when the Chamber of Deputies approved the re-election bill, despite opposition among allied parties.

O Globo reported, however, that some senators who want to run for state governorships in 1998 might try to alter the bill by insisting that holders of executive officer step down six months before seeking re-election.
"Nearly 40 senators will be candidates next year and (if their rivals are allowed to stay in office while campaigning) they have got no chance of winning," senator Ernandes Amorim said.
